answer: Only 69% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. Because the spiral ledger attributes every share, the meadow audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it burns the echo fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 28 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
